title: Connect it to the work
prompt: Ticket (scrubbed): "Customers say the CSV export times out on big accounts. Make it faster." You have the repo. Before writing any code: what does done mean, what would you ask, and what is your first step?

standin.solo: The goal is that a full export for the largest accounts finishes without timing out. I'd ask how big the biggest accounts are and whether customers need the file right away or can get an emailed link. First step: reproduce it on staging with a large seeded account and measure a baseline, so we know what faster means.
standin.team: Adding to that: one more question is whether the export can stream rows instead of building the whole file in memory, because that changes the design. The risk is breaking existing integrations that parse the file, so the format stays the same.

title: Judge the output

standin.solo: I would not approve it. DAY is in seconds but Date.now() is in milliseconds, so the cutoff is only about 43 minutes ago. The job deletes almost every record, which is data loss in an audit table. The fix: DAY should be 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000. I'd also add a test with records on both sides of the cutoff, not an empty fixture.
standin.team: The cutoff math is the problem: DAY is in seconds and Date.now() is in milliseconds. Before it runs in production I'd add a dry run that logs the row count it would delete, and an alert if that count is far above the usual nightly number.

title: Work within limits
prompt: You can read the repo, the application logs and staging. Production database access is off-limits for this exercise. The slow export seems tied to one large account. How do you investigate, and what would you need from someone else?

standin.solo: Production data is off-limits, so I won't query it. I'd start with the application logs for that account's export requests and the query timings, then rebuild a similar data shape on staging and profile the export there. If I need row counts for that account I'd ask the database owner for them, because that tells us if it is volume or a slow query.
standin.team: I can take staging: seed an account at a similar size and profile it, so we can compare with what the logs show.

title: Own the result
prompt: Your export change shipped. Thirty minutes later the export error rate is roughly double. Walk me through the next hour: rollback, what you would monitor, and what you would tell stakeholders.

standin.solo: First, turn off the flag or revert the change so customers get the old behavior back. Then watch the export error rate and latency dashboards to confirm they return to the baseline. I'd post an update in the incident channel and let support know what changed and when it was fixed.
standin.team: While that rollback runs I'll watch the error rate dashboard and confirm it drops. Afterward I'd write up the root cause and add a new test for the failing case so it is caught next time.
